title: Sunny and the Tawny Frogmouth
author: Jamie Wigg
the_end_text:
The End.
Sweet dreams, little one. Goodnight.
back_cover_blurb: Deep in the hushed evening bush, Sunny the little quokka meets a tawny frogmouth sitting so still he looks just like a branch. He shows her the quiet magic of being still and watching the night. A calm, cosy bedtime tale for winding down and drifting off to sleep. Perfect for little ones ages 1-5.

pages.scene: the little quokka walking softly beneath tall old gum trees in the deep blue evening, the bush very quiet and still, first stars and a soft honey glow on the horizon
pages.text: Deep in the quiet evening bush, Sunny walked beneath the tall gum trees. Everything was hushed and still.

pages.scene: the little quokka looking up curiously at a knobbly branch of a gum tree that looks a little odd, dusk light, wondering
pages.text: She looked up at a branch. Was it a broken branch… or something else?

pages.scene: a tawny frogmouth bird with big round golden-yellow eyes slowly opening, mottled grey-brown feathers, perched on the branch, the little quokka gazing up surprised and delighted
pages.text: Two big golden eyes slowly opened. It was a tawny frogmouth!

pages.scene: close view of the tawny frogmouth with soft mottled grey and brown feathers exactly like tree bark, sitting on the branch, the little quokka watching from below
pages.text: His feathers were mottled grey and brown, exactly like the old tree bark.

pages.scene: the little quokka smiling up at the tawny frogmouth who blinks one golden eye, friendly, moonlit gum tree
pages.text: “I didn't see you at all,” said Sunny. “That's the idea,” he blinked.

pages.scene: the tawny frogmouth sitting perfectly still on the branch looking just like a part of the tree, the little quokka tilting her head, gentle night
pages.text: He sat so very still, he looked just like part of the tree.

pages.scene: a gentle portrait of the tawny frogmouth with a wide soft beak, bark-like feathers, big calm golden eyes, perfectly still on the branch, the little quokka nearby
pages.text: A wide soft beak, feathers like old bark, and eyes as gold as the moon.

pages.scene: the tawny frogmouth on his branch at night looking out patiently over the moonlit bush, the little quokka listening below
pages.text: “At night I sit, and watch, and wait, and listen,” he said softly.

pages.scene: the tawny frogmouth tipping his head back with his beak pointed up to the starry sky, looking thin as a twig, the little quokka watching in wonder
pages.text: He tipped his head right back, thin as a twig against the stars.

pages.scene: the hushed moonlit bush with tall gum trees, a soft breeze in the leaves, the little quokka and the still frogmouth, deeply peaceful
pages.text: The bush was hushed and calm. Only the soft wind whispered by.

pages.scene: a single moth fluttering softly in the moonlight, the tawny frogmouth's golden eyes following it calmly and patiently, the little quokka beside the tree
pages.text: A little moth fluttered past. The frogmouth watched, calm and patient.

pages.scene: the tawny frogmouth speaking gently to the little quokka in the moonlit bush, warm and wise, fireflies starting to glow
pages.text: “Being still,” he said, “is a kind of quiet magic.”

pages.scene: the little quokka trying to sit very still and calm just like the frogmouth, eyes soft, in the moonlit grass beneath the branch
pages.text: So Sunny tried to sit very still too, quiet as the frogmouth.

pages.scene: the little quokka and the tawny frogmouth together watching the stars come out over the gum trees, calm and content, soft night
pages.text: Together they watched the stars come softly out, one by one.

pages.scene: glowing fireflies drifting through the bush and a silver moon rising over the tall gum trees, the little quokka and frogmouth peaceful
pages.text: Fireflies drifted by, and the moon rose silver over the gums.

pages.scene: the tawny frogmouth giving a low soft purring call with his beak, gentle sound in the calm night, the little quokka listening sleepily
pages.text: The frogmouth gave a low, soft, purring call. Oom… oom… oom.

pages.scene: the little quokka growing sleepy, eyes half closed, soothed by the stillness of the moonlit bush, the frogmouth calm on his branch
pages.text: The gentle stillness made Sunny's eyes grow heavy and slow.

pages.scene: the little quokka whispering goodnight up to the tawny frogmouth who blinks his golden eyes kindly, tender moonlit moment
pages.text: “Goodnight,” whispered Sunny. The frogmouth blinked his golden eyes.

pages.scene: the little quokka padding softly home through the cool quiet moonlit grass beneath the gum trees, sleepy and calm, stars above
pages.text: Softly, softly, Sunny padded home through the cool night grass.

pages.scene: the little quokka fast asleep and peaceful in her cosy leaf nest with a gentle smile, moon and stars glowing, a tawny frogmouth still and calm on a far branch
pages.text: She curled up warm, and slept, and dreamed of golden eyes and quiet branches.
